lines.text: I neglected? Who is looking to me for help? Who longs to
hear a kind word from me? We should not let our attention
be dissipated in the noise and bustle of the day, in the cares
of our work, in our joys and sorrows. We should not forget
to notice what God now and then wishes to say to us!
To be sure, God's call is as a rule very inconvenient to us.
When we are called to help anyone it rarely fits in with our
personal situation. We have no time, our work is so pressing!
We are constantly expected to give out and we have not
enough ourselves. It is true that there is so much distress
that we cannot help everybody. But have we always done as
much as we could? Have we at least always had a friendly
glance, a kind word when we were approached? Or if any-
one wants anything from us, do we always feel it to be a
horrid disturbance?
But it is not merely the need of our fellow men in which
God's call to us is heard. It may also be our own need, our
own fate, which strikes us down and makes us shiver with
dismay. When our lives go according to our plans and
wishes, when life brings attractive work for our powers, and
when our work is crowned with success and joy, then our
world seems to be irradiated as from within by its own light.
In such circumstances it is easy for us to forget that the light
which illuminates our path really falls on our world from
without, that it is the light of the goodness of God, that it
streams upon us as sunlight on the earth. And just as the
sun can be hidden behind clouds as the sun sets, so also our
world gladdened by congenial tasks and the pride of success
may once again be plunged in darkness.
When this happens our world can grow sinister and un-
canny, and the activities of all men including our own begin
to seem strange and purposeless. If such a fate strikes us, in
one way or another, then it is God who is confronting us
anew. But shall we be able to recognize Him in this mysteri-
ous darkness? Shall we hear His call in the terrible silence of
